text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lawyers in Blantyre said on Tuesday the many cases pending judgment for several years and failure by the sheriff's office to enforce court judgments were making a mockery of the country's judicial system.

- The wage dispute between civil servants and government goes back to the negotiating table on Thursday after disgruntled civil servants decided to call off their strike in its seventh week on Tuesday.

- Civil Servants Trade Union (CSTU) president Thomas Banda on Tuesday announced the end of the nationwide strike because government had agreed to withdraw all interdictions, dismissals, forced transfers and court cases.

- Political parties are now coming up with tangible evidence on irregularities involving voter registration certificates, pending by-elections scheduled for May 26, Electoral Commission chairperson Anastazia Msosa said on Tuesday.

- The civil servants strike which had entered its seventh week was on Tuesday called off following amicable preliminary talks between the government and civil servants' union leaders convened by the umbrella Malawi Congress of Trade Unions.

- There is mounting animosity between Lands and Valuation Minister Peter Fachi and the leader of the opposition, Gwanda Chakuamba, as the days draw closer for a by-election in their Lower Shire home area.
